newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain opposition cleric dies in prison. [CORRECTED 07:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bahrain opposition cleric dies in prison. [CORRECTED 07:10 GMT]

text.p: Bahrain's government has said a blind opposition cleric died in prison from natural causes and denied claims by exiled groups that he was tortured.

"An official at the Interior Ministry said the death of Ali Merza al-Nachas was a natural one because of respiratory difficulties which he had suffered for a while," Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said late on Sunday.
"It was proved in the medical examination...that the death was natural because of the illness he suffered. The family of the deceased has been informed of his natural death."
The agency did not give details of when Nachas was detained or when he died.

An exiled opposition group, the Bahrain Freedom Movement said in a statement sent to an international news agency that Nachas, 50, died on Sunday from ill-treatment and torture. (Corrects to make clear statement was sent by only one group.)
They said Nachas was first detained in January 1996 and released in February 1997. He was detained again in March for delivering anti-government political sermons at mosques.
More than two dozen people have been killed in over two years of anti-government protests in the Gulf Arab state. Hundreds of people have been arrested.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to implement economic and political reforms.
